description: Canonical searchQueryIndex test vectors. Every Tracive SDK (Kotlin, Flutter, Swift) and the Tracive API MUST produce byte-identical output for these inputs. This file is vendored verbatim into each SDK repository and is the anti-drift contract between them.

derivedFrom.authority: Generated by executing the Tracive API's own canonical key normalizer, not transcribed by hand. If an SDK disagrees with a vector here, the SDK is wrong.
derivedFrom.note: The server also folds caller-supplied keys on the read path, so a key differing only in casing or whitespace still resolves. SDKs fold locally anyway: the folded key is also the local cache key, and an unfolded key would split one entity into several cache entries.

rules.PHONE: PHONE_<value>. Strip every character that is not a digit, preserving a single leading '+'. No case folding (digits only). SDKs additionally REJECT anything that is not E.164 after stripping (^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$) — the server does not reconcile a local-format number against its E.164 form, so a local number silently becomes a different entity and the miss is still billed.
rules.EMAIL: EMAIL_<value>. Unicode NFC, then lowercase, then trim (in that order).
rules.BANK_IBAN: BANK_IBAN_<accountId>. accountId: uppercase, then remove every whitespace character and ASCII hyphen. Note: uppercase happens BEFORE stripping, and NFC is NOT applied.
rules.BANK_COUNTRY: BANK_<country>_<bankCode>_<accountId>. country: uppercase+trim, must be ISO 3166-1 alpha-3. bankCode: NFC, uppercase, trim, then remove every underscore (the id is split on '_', so an underscore would corrupt the parse). accountId: same fold as BANK_IBAN.
rules.CRYPTO: CRYPTO_<chain>_<address>. chain: NFC, uppercase, trim. address: trim, then lowercase IF AND ONLY IF it matches ^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ (an EVM address). Base58 addresses are case-sensitive and must NOT be folded.
rules.USERNAME: USERNAME_<platform>_<handle>. platform: NFC, uppercase, trim. handle: NFC, lowercase, trim. A leading '@' is NOT stripped — the server preserves it, so stripping it client-side would build a key that misses.

crossLanguageSemantics.$comment: The Tracive API folds keys with JavaScript string semantics. To be byte-identical you must reimplement those, NOT your platform's defaults. Every item below was verified by executing the reference implementation.

trimSet.note: JS String.prototype.trim() strips EXACTLY this set. Hand-write this character class — do not use your platform's trim().
trimSet.platformTraps: Kotlin Regex("\\s") is ASCII-only and Kotlin trim() does not strip U+FEFF. Swift/ICU NSRegularExpression \s omits U+000B and U+FEFF. Dart's trim() follows Unicode WhiteSpace, which differs at U+FEFF.

digitSet.note: JS \D is exactly [^0-9] (ASCII). Arabic-Indic and other Unicode digits are STRIPPED, never converted.
digitSet.platformTraps: ICU \d is Unicode Nd, so an NSRegularExpression phone normalizer would KEEP Arabic-Indic digits the backend removes. Filter on ASCII 0-9 explicitly.

caseMapping.note: JS toLowerCase()/toUpperCase() are locale-INVARIANT full case mappings and can change string length.
caseMapping.platformTraps: Kotlin: use uppercase()/lowercase() with NO Locale argument (uppercase(Locale.getDefault()) breaks under the Turkish locale). Swift: uppercased()/lowercased(), never a locale variant. Dart: toUpperCase()/toLowerCase().

crossLanguageSemantics.nfcScope: NFC is applied to email, username, platform and chain codes ONLY. It is NOT applied to bank account ids, crypto addresses or phone numbers.
crossLanguageSemantics.foldOrder: Order is part of the contract. email/username: NFC -> lowercase -> trim. platform/chain/bank code: NFC -> uppercase -> trim. bank account: uppercase -> strip [\s-] (NO separate trim). crypto address: trim -> conditional lowercase. Reordering changes output on edge inputs.
crossLanguageSemantics.phoneFolding: The server folds PHONE on the read path, but SDKs MUST fold it client-side regardless: the folded key is also the local cache key, so an unfolded one would split a single entity across several cache entries and defeat the cache-hit path entirely. Never rely on the server to fold on your behalf.

documentIdGuard.$comment: Applied server-side to the FOLDED key (folding runs first because case mapping is not length-preserving). Mirror it client-side so a doomed key never costs a credit.

notImplemented.DOMAIN: The Tracive API indexes exactly five identifier types: PHONE, EMAIL, BANK, CRYPTO and USERNAME. There is no DOMAIN type, so a DOMAIN_<host> key would match nothing — and a miss is still billed. SDKs MUST NOT expose a domain() query builder. Domain checking is planned for a future release built on vector similarity search (typosquatting, homoglyphs, subdomain permutation), which does not fit exact-match document ids; adding it later is not a breaking change.

vectors.why: Formatting punctuation is stripped so every printed form collapses to one key.
Decomposed 'e' + U+0301 combining acute must NFC-compose to U+00E9, otherwise one address indexes as two entities.
TC-I14: a dashed and an undashed account number are the same account.
The id is split on '_', so underscores are stripped from the bank code defensively.
IBANs are printed in groups of four; the spaces are presentational.
EIP-55 checksum casing is presentational; record keys are case-sensitive.
Base58 is case-SENSITIVE: lowercasing yields a different, invalid address. Base58 excludes '0', so it can never collide with the 0x EVM test.
bech32 is not folded: its regex admits only the lowercase form, so the other case never reaches the index.
The server does NOT strip a leading '@' (normalizeUsernameValue only folds NFC/case/whitespace). Stripping it client-side would build a key that misses a report filed with the '@'.
USERNAME is split on the FIRST underscore only, so underscores in the handle round-trip.
JS trim() strips U+00A0. A bank-statement or PDF paste carries NBSP. Kotlin trim() also strips it, but a hand-rolled ASCII-only class would not.
JS trim() does NOT strip U+200B (ZWSP). Mirroring the server means keeping it, even though the key then misses — matching the server is the contract, not guessing what the user meant.
U+0130 lowercases to 'i' + U+0307 COMBINING DOT ABOVE under the locale-invariant mapping. Passing a Turkish locale would produce plain 'i' and a different key.
Pinned by a backend test. The /[\s-]/ class includes U+00A0; Kotlin's Regex("\\s") is ASCII-only and would leave the NBSP in.
Case mapping is length-changing: 'ß' uppercases to 'SS'. This is also why the 1500-byte guard must run AFTER folding.
Underscores are deliberately kept in the account (the id is split on '_' but everything past the bank code is rejoined).
JS \D is ASCII [^0-9], so U+0669 ARABIC-INDIC NINE is REMOVED, not converted to '9'. An ICU-based \d port would keep it and build a different key.

The EVM test regex requires a LOWERCASE '0x' prefix, so an uppercase '0X' address is not folded. The write path applies the same rule, so the two sides still agree — mirror it exactly rather than 'fixing' it.

rejected.why: The server does not up-convert a local number to E.164 (it cannot know the dial code at that layer). Sending it would create a different entity and be billed as a miss.
E.164 country codes never start with 0.
The server would up-convert ID to IDN, but the SDK requires alpha-3 so the local cache key matches the server key exactly. Callers must pass alpha-3.
The write path drops a row with an empty account id, so such a key can never hit.
A record key cannot contain '/'. Guarded before the request is sent.
